deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Grothendieck is working in a 'tame' context: PL, semi-algebraic or subanalytic spaces. On the previous page he decided to work with equisingular partitions into leaves (strata) rather than filtrations. He defined an admissible system of partitions on a diagram of spaces X = (X_i)_{i in I}. The conditions are that each partition is admissible and that every map X_i -> X_j coming from an arrow i -> j sends each leaf of X_i into a unique leaf of X_j.

This page, step 1 (an auxiliary diagram). Let 𝔏_i be the set of leaves of X_i, ordered by inclusion of closures (the frontier-condition order: α ≤ β iff F_α ⊂ closure(F_β)). Each arrow i -> j induces an order-preserving map 𝔏_i -> 𝔏_j, so (𝔏_i)_{i in I} is a diagram of type I of posets. Its 'evident' total indexing category is in modern terms the Grothendieck construction (category of elements) ∫_I 𝔏. Its objects are pairs (i, α) and its arrows combine inclusions of leaf closures with the maps X_i -> X_j. Over this category one gets a new diagram of spaces (i, α) ↦ closure(F_{i,α}). Its maps closure(F_{i,α}) -> closure(F_{j,β}) are restrictions of the maps X_i -> X_j and of the inclusions of closures.

Step 2 (equisingularity for diagrams). The system of partitions is called equisingular relative to X if this diagram of closed leaves is equisingular along every leaf of every X_i. This uses a notion of equisingularity of a diagram along a subspace, presumably defined on earlier pages: local triviality of the whole diagram structure along a leaf.

Step 3 (margin definition). A system of partitions is 'privileged' if it is equisingular and, in addition, the leaves of every X_i (or their closures, depending on the reading) are (connected) manifolds. These are stratifications in the modern sense, locally trivial along strata, for a whole diagram at once.

Step 4 (Conjecture 1). In the PL, semi-algebraic or analytic piecewise context:
- every space X admits a privileged partition;
- among all privileged partitions there is a coarsest one, called 'canonical'.

This is the existence of a canonical, intrinsic, minimal stratification of a tame space by local (tame) topological type.

Purpose. Next page: one needs privileged partitions refining given data or compatible with maps. This leads to Conjecture 2: finite poset diagrams with proper maps admit a coarsest privileged partition. The whole serves the 'dévissage' programme of tame topology later sketched in Esquisse d'un programme.
errors: The definition is partly circular as written. 'Equisingular along a leaf' for a diagram of closed leaves presupposes a notion of equisingularity for diagrams that must be defined independently, presumably on earlier pages, as local triviality along a subspace.

For 𝔏_i -> 𝔏_j to be order-preserving one needs the frontier condition. From F_α ⊂ closure(F_β) one only gets that the image leaf of α meets the closure of the image leaf of β. Admissibility must therefore include the frontier condition; this is implicit, not stated on this page.

If the margin really says that the closures of leaves are manifolds, the condition is too strong: the closure of an open stratum of a cone is not a manifold. The natural and probably intended condition is that the leaves themselves are connected manifolds.

In Conjecture 1, 'coarsest' requires that the set of privileged partitions is closed under some common-coarsening operation. This holds for intrinsic stratifications by local topological type but is not argued here; it is a conjecture, so this is not an error.

ideas.what: Diagram of leaf posets (𝔏_i)_{i∈I} and the induced diagram of closed leaves indexed by the total category
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck construction / category of elements of a functor I -> Posets; diagrams of poset-stratified spaces (cf. stratified spaces over a poset, exit-path formalism)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck construction: Grothendieck (SGA1, 1960s). Poset-stratified spaces as functorial objects: Lurie (Higher Algebra, appendix A), Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2010s).
ideas.where_published: Not as such; Esquisse d'un programme (1984) mentions stratified tame structures only in outline.

ideas.what: Equisingular (locally trivial) system of partitions on a diagram of spaces, defined via the diagram of closed leaves
ideas.modern_name: Simultaneous (Thom–Mather / Hardt-type) stratification of a diagram of maps; stratified maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom, Mather (stratified maps, isotopy lemmas, 1960s–70s); Hardt (semi-algebraic triviality, 1980)
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 (tame topology, dévissage); no precise definition published.

ideas.modern_name: Locally (topologically/PL) trivial stratification; CS-set or conelike stratification

ideas.what: Conjecture 1: existence of privileged partitions and of a coarsest ('canonical') one
ideas.modern_name: Intrinsic / canonical minimal stratification by local topological type
ideas.usually_credited_to: PL intrinsic stratification: Akin (1969), Armstrong. Topological: Sullivan, King (1985), Friedman (book). Minimal Whitney stratification: Mather, Teissier (1982). Existence of tame stratifications: Łojasiewicz, Hironaka, Hardt.
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses canonical tame stratifications in spirit; unsure whether this exact statement appears.

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates equisingularity and canonical coarsest stratifications for whole diagrams of tame spaces, indexing the closed strata by the Grothendieck construction of the leaf posets. He conjectures a coarsest privileged partition. The single-space case is essentially known (intrinsic stratifications). A systematic treatment of canonical coarsest locally trivial stratifications of arbitrary finite diagrams, done functorially via ∫_I 𝔏_i, does not seem standard. This is developed in the follow-up Conjecture 2 on the next page.
missed.quote: Parmi toutes les partitions privilégiées de X, il en est une plus grossière que toutes les autres (appelée "canonique").
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This links tame stratification theory with the modern functorial view of stratified spaces as diagrams over posets (exit paths, constructible sheaves). Canonical stratifications of diagrams would make such constructions functorial in maps.

missed.claim: Indexing the closed strata of a diagram of stratified spaces by the category of elements of I -> Posets anticipates the later practice of treating stratified spaces as spaces over posets and diagrams thereof.
missed.quote: un nouveau diagramme (dont le type se déduit de façon évidente du type de diagramme I, des ensembles ordonnés par inclusion des 𝔏_i des feuilles
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly historical interest: it shows Grothendieck in 1974 already treating stratifications as poset-indexed diagrammatic data.

deep.surprise_reason: These are clean unpublished definitions in Grothendieck's 1974 tame-topology notes. The canonical-stratification conjecture for single spaces is essentially known (Akin, King, Mather, Teissier). The diagram-level formulation is a notable but not shocking detail, and it largely fits what Esquisse later sketches.
transcription_corrections: The leaf sets are written with a script/fraktur L, $\mathfrak{L}_i$ (consistent with the $\mathcal{L}$ used on the next page), not $\mathfrak{P}_i$. The same applies to the morphisms $\mathfrak{L}_i \to \mathfrak{L}_j$ and the inserted $(\mathfrak{L}_i)_{i\in I}$.

Margin: the subject of 'sont des variétés (connexes)' appears to be the leaves ('feuilles' inserted above the line). 'les adhérences des feuilles' is doubtful; the mathematically natural reading is 'les feuilles de tout X_i sont des variétés (connexes)'.
The inserted word read as 'produit[?]' sits above the struck-out 's'il est admissible, et si'; the reading is uncertain (possibly 'pourvu que' or similar).
The handwritten page number is 35, while the archive numbering gives page 33.
